Convert a (Tree)SummarizedExperiment to a phyloseq object

Source: R/mp_import.R
mp_as_phyloseq.Rd

Bioconductor's microbiome stack (mia, miaViz, the OMA book) stores data in a TreeSummarizedExperiment rather than a phyloseq object. Every mp_*() function calls this conversion on its input, so either container can be passed directly; it is exported for when you want the phyloseq object itself.

Usage

mp_as_phyloseq(x, assay.type = NULL)

Arguments

x

A TreeSummarizedExperiment or SummarizedExperiment; a phyloseq object is returned unchanged.

assay.type

Name of the assay holding the counts. Defaults to "counts" when present, otherwise the first assay.

Value

A phyloseq::phyloseq object.

Details

The count assay becomes the OTU table, colData() the sample data, the taxonomic-rank columns of rowData() the taxonomy table and, for a TreeSummarizedExperiment, rowTree() the phylogeny (pruned and relabelled to the rows it links to). Non-atomic colData() columns, which phyloseq cannot hold, are dropped.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("TreeSummarizedExperiment", quietly = TRUE)) {
  counts <- matrix(rpois(40, 20), nrow = 5,
                   dimnames = list(paste0("OTU", 1:5), paste0("S", 1:8)))
  tse <- TreeSummarizedExperiment::TreeSummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    rowData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(Phylum = rep(c("A", "B"), c(2, 3))),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(Group = rep(c("x", "y"), 4)))
  mp_as_phyloseq(tse)
}
#> phyloseq-class experiment-level object
#> otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 5 taxa and 8 samples ]
#> sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 8 samples by 1 sample variables ]
#> tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 5 taxa by 1 taxonomic ranks ]
